science.title: Generative AI for efficient statistical computation of fluids
science.description: We present GenCFD, a generative modeling approach for fast, accurate, and robust statistical computation of three-dimensional turbulent fluid flows. While motivated from conditional score-based diffusion models, GenCFD is both empirically and theoretically validated on generating turbulent flows. Extensive numerical experimentation of challenging three-dimensional fluids demonstrates that GenCFD provides an accurate approximation of relevant statistical quantities of interest while also efficiently generating high-quality realistic samples of such flows. Moreover, we present rigorous theoretical results on analytically tractable models with mathematically relevant features of turbulent fluid flows. The analysis uncovers the mechanism underlying the success of the diffusion modeling approach. In particular, we highlight the importance of modeling distributions by GenCFD, while the mean-square-loss used by the deterministic machine learning approaches fails to accurately characterize statistical features of chaotic dynamics. Turbulent fluid dynamics pose a formidable computational challenge: chaotic, multiscale Navier–Stokes solutions require large ensembles for reliable statistical estimates, making direct numerical simulation intractable for many high–Reynolds-number problems. This work demonstrates that generative AI models, specifically diffusion-based approaches, can efficiently produce statistically accurate samples of complex three-dimensional turbulent fluid flows, surpassing traditional deterministic neural surrogates that tend to regress to mean behavior.

science.title: Metabolites derived from cell signaling pathways modulate AMPK-dependent autophagic flux in disease-relevant cell models under cellular stress conditions
science.description: Autophagy is a critical adaptive response to metabolic stress that is closely associated with AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling. This study investigated the effects of the physiologically relevant dietary metabolites sodium acetate and resveratrol on AMPK-associated autophagic flux and oxidative stress in primary human fibroblasts, HepG2 hepatocytes, and SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells subjected to nutrient deprivation. Using bafilomycin A1-sensitive LC3-II turnover assays, pharmacological inhibition, and cellular ROS measurements, we found that both metabolites significantly enhanced autophagic flux in a time- and concentration-dependent manner, with maximal responses observed at 200 µM acetate and 1 µM resveratrol. Pharmacological evidence supported the involvement of AMPK signaling in these responses, which were also associated with marked reductions in mitochondrial superoxide and total intracellular ROS. Importantly, these cytoprotective effects were observed at physiologically relevant concentrations, without compromising lysosomal integrity, and were closely associated with enhanced autophagic activity rather than direct radical scavenging. Collectively, our findings suggest that sodium acetate and resveratrol may act as modulators of AMPK-associated autophagy and redox homeostasis, providing mechanistic support for their potential nutraceutical applications in metabolic and age-related disorders.

science.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of urban noise complaints link emotion, space, and management pathways
science.description: Noise pollution is a critical urban environmental issue with significant public health implications, and public complaints serve as a key indicator of resident dissatisfaction. Emotional analysis has been widely used to evaluate the emotional factors behind public complaints. However, existing studies have focused primarily on atmospheric pollution-related complaints, while little attention has been paid to noise complaints, despite the fact that the emotional descriptions in noise complaints differ notably from those associated with other types of complaints. This study employs sentiment analysis in combination with traditional temporal and spatial analysis to investigate the spatiotemporal patterns of emotions expressed in online noise complaints, using Guangzhou—a city with a high incidence of noise complaints—as a case study. The results revealed two distinct yet interrelated patterns. On one hand, noise complaints exhibit a consistent temporal rhythm: winter and weekdays register the highest volumes, shaped by cultural customs and daily routines, with pronounced surges during both daytime and late-night hours. On the other hand, a pronounced spatial mismatch exists between complaint density and emotional intensity. While complaints are concentrated in the central city, the most acute negative sentiments emerge in newly developing zones characterized by urban-rural and port-industry-city integration. This study not only assists Guangzhou—a typical first-tier city in China—in its noise pollution management, but also highlights that incorporating public sentiment into urban noise management can help uncover latent stress patterns and management blind spots that are often overlooked in conventional approaches.

science.title: 3D-printed meta-matching layer for enhanced ultrasound transmission through calcified plaques: a phantom study
science.description: Calcified plaques strongly reflect ultrasound waves, limiting visualization of structures located behind them. This proof-of-concept work presents one of the first demonstrations of a directly 3D-printed meta-matching layer (MML) designed for medical ultrasound frequencies (4 MHz) to improve transmission through calcified plaque-like structures. The MML employs subwavelength microstructures to create a gradient acoustic impedance, reducing reflections and enhancing acoustic transmission. Numerical optimization and experimental validation demonstrated strong agreement. At 4 MHz, the optimized 10-$$\mu$$m-resolution MML increased relative transmission by approximately 192% and reduced relative reflection by approximately 77% compared with the aberrating layer alone. Ultrasound imaging confirmed improved signal penetration into the vessel lumen and preservation of downstream vessel visibility. Although image artifacts introduced by the structured interface currently limit robust flow quantification, this proof-of-concept study demonstrates the feasibility of patient-specific, add-on metamaterial layers for enhancing ultrasound transmission through highly reflective vascular structures.

science.title: Derivation of human post-mitotic cardiomyocytes from tetraploid iPSCs
science.description: Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cardiomyocytes (iPS-CMs) have great potential in regenerative medicine. However, iPS-CMs are immature and resemble fetal cardiomyocytes, restricting their application. Fetal cardiomyocytes in the human heart are diploid and proliferating, but gradually lose their proliferative potential during maturation. Most human cardiomyocytes eventually become tetraploid, but iPS-CMs cannot replicate this tetraploidization and remain immature with the current differentiation techniques. To overcome this problem, we fused diploid iPSCs to establish tetraploid iPSCs and differentiated them into cardiomyocytes (4N-iPS-CMs) to replicate the tetraploidy. As we expected, we found that 4N-iPS-CMs had more similar gene expression profiles, improved mitochondrial functions, contractile impedance, and resistance to a potassium blocker in post-mitotic cardiomyocytes than conventional iPS-CMs. In addition, we successfully generated 4N-iPS-CMs from two individuals to mix two different genetic backgrounds. Thus, we demonstrated a unique strategy for generating human post-mitotic cardiomyocyte-like cells by generating tetraploid iPSCs. Cardiomyocytes derived from tetraploid iPSCs established by cell fusion recapitulate characteristics of post-mitotic cardiomyocytes more precisely than conventional diploid iPSC derived cardiomyocytes.

science.title: Mixed positive and negative feedback loops drive diverse single-cell gene expression dynamics
science.description: Genetic circuits with only a few components can generate complex gene regulatory dynamics. Here, we combine stochastic modelling and single-cell time-lapse microscopy to map how a common circuit motif, the mixed positive/negative feedback loop, gives rise to diverse single-cell behaviours. Our minimal stochastic model of this motif reveals ten distinct classes of dynamic output, including stochastic pulsing, oscillations, and bistability. We systematically map how the circuit’s core parameters can be tuned to generate each of the behaviours. Experimental validation in two different mixed feedback circuits in the bacterium Bacillus subtilis, σB and σV, confirms our model’s predictive power. Guided by our simulations, we are able to transition between selected dynamic behaviours by modulating in vivo parameters. Together, these results establish a quantitative framework for how mixed feedback loops generate diverse single-cell dynamics, improving our understanding of this common biological network motif and informing our efforts to engineer them for synthetic biology applications. A simple genetic circuit can generate complex gene regulatory dynamics. Here the authors use modelling and time-lapse microscopy to map how the mixed positive/negative feedback loop gives rise to ten distinct classes of single-cell behaviours.
